> **Dana** · reviewer · owns the eval harness

One thing worth adding for people arriving from a search or platform background rather than an ML one.

The instinct here is to read the toolkit first — `store.py`, `retrieve.py` — because that is where the code you recognise lives. **Read [notebook 01](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/notebooks/01_retrieval_and_evaluation_foundations.ipynb) first anyway.** The whole repository is organised around the idea that a number without an interval is an anecdote, and if you skip the measurement material the retrieval code looks over-engineered — you cannot see what the harness is protecting against.

Fastest path if you have an hour: notebook 01 end to end, then §1.3 twice.

> **Priya** · cohort peer

Practical note for anyone who hits it: `make lab` on a fresh machine wants the dev extras, and `pip install -e .` alone is not enough — you want `make setup` or `pip install -e ".[dev]"`. Cost me ten minutes before I read the Makefile.

Also worth saying out loud since it took me a while to believe it: there really is no dataset download and no API key. If you are waiting for something to install, you have gone wrong somewhere.
